summary: Retest of the 3 iter-16 fixes for Vendor→Substore transfer flow. 2 of 3 fixes VERIFIED working (accepted_at now populated; new 'Received via substore transfer' panel renders on /vendor/substore for the receiving vendor). The 3rd fix (hydration warning '<span> cannot be a child of <option>') is NOT resolved at runtime — however the source-code change is technically correct. Root cause is Emergent's runtime visual-editor instrumentation which auto-wraps every JSX `{expression}` in a `<span style="display:contents" data-ve-dynamic="true">`, and this wrapping fires for BOTH the product picker option and the destination-substore option (which has `{s.name} · {s.email}`) — not user-fixable in the component code.

Open issue: hydration warning at runtime is caused by preview-env visual-editor wrapping ALL JSX {expr} inside <option> in `<span data-ve-dynamic style=display:contents>` — verified in DOM dump. Not fixable in the component source; needs preview-env fix or accept as noise. The DOM inspection was done on support@'s modal after seeding a substore.
rca of the issue: Hydration warning still present at runtime despite E1's correct code change. Investigation: dumped outerHTML of both <select> options in the New Transfer modal. Found that Emergent's runtime instrumentation (attribute `data-ve-dynamic="true"`, `x-file-name`, `x-line-number`, `x-component`) auto-wraps every JSX expression like {p.name} / {s.email} in `<span style="display:contents">`. This wrapper is not present in the source and cannot be removed by using template literals inside {…} — a lone {priceStr} expression still becomes a wrapped span. Same instrumentation also wraps the destination-substore option's {s.name} and {s.email}. Because React still sees a real HTML `<span>` DOM child of `<option>`, it emits the hydration warning. Recommendation: either skip <option> children in the visual-editor tag injector, or move away from {expr} children of <option> entirely (impractical). Functionally the app behaves correctly — this is a dev-console warning only.
